title: I Bought the 2020 Crash. I'm Doing It Again With This Plan
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Brian lays out his crash-buy plan after the Nasdaq 100 suffered its worst day since March 2020, noting that buying on a 4%+ down day was higher a year later in 12 of 15 such sell-offs over 30 years, with a typical gain of about 18%. He keeps 5-10% of his portfolio as dry powder and only deploys it into stocks that pass three tests: they fell about as much as the Nasdaq that day, they trade below fair value, and they have a three-year growth outlook. His $100 split is $70 to big names, $25 to midsize and $5 to small caps. On Thursday he bought TSMC (TSM, down ~11%, sales +41%, 3-year forecast ~25%/yr), ASML (down ~9%, sales +55%, ~26%/yr) and AMD (down ~7%, data-centre business nearly doubled, $100B+ OpenAI deal, ~49%/yr). Also on the list: NVDA (conditional — already ~12% of his portfolio, so he did not add), Lam Research (LRCX), Credo (CRDO), Astera Labs (ALAB), IonQ (IONQ), Rambus (RMBS) and Cohu (COHU). Apple is explicitly excluded — it fell only ~1.5% and his 3-year forecast is just ~12%/yr. He notes IREN and Oklo bounced hardest on Friday but failed his checklist. Calls: TSM BUY, ASML BUY, AMD BUY, LRCX BUY, CRDO BUY, ALAB BUY, IONQ BUY, RMBS BUY, COHU BUY (all first tracked except IONQ and RMBS), NVDA CONDITIONAL_BUY (softened from BUY on position size).
